claim: A job that always raises ValueError is run 3 times in total, with pauses of 1 and 2 seconds between the runs. A job that raises KeyError is run once.
why: The README says up to 3 retries with pauses 1, 2 and 4, but the loop makes 3 attempts in total and sleeps only between attempts, so the pauses are 1 and 2. Only ValueError is caught, so a KeyError escapes on the first run. The trap is a reader who trusts the README (4 runs, 3 pauses) and rejects a claim that the code supports.

deciding.note: KeyError is not caught, so one run

root.claim: A job that always raises ValueError runs 3 times with pauses 1 and 2; a KeyError job runs once.

atoms.claim: An always-failing ValueError job is run 3 times in total.
atoms.evidence: retry.run loops range(3) and catches ValueError; main.py prints calls: 3.

atoms.claim: The pauses between the runs are 1 and 2 seconds.
atoms.evidence: sleep is called only when n < attempts - 1 with base * 2**n; main.py prints pauses: [1, 2].

atoms.claim: A job that raises KeyError is run once.
atoms.evidence: Only ValueError is caught, so a KeyError propagates from the first call.
